findings.mechanism: BufferPool.free retains every buffer returned by Put, with no cap and no release. It grows to the largest batch size seen (maxBatch=400 buffers, a few KB each) and then stops.
findings.cause: high-water-mark retention by design in a pool; not unbounded growth
findings.evidence: Ran 6000 batches with a scratch test (not committed), forcing GC and reading HeapAlloc every 1000 batches. Pool created/idle count was 79 at batch 0 and 400/400 from batch 1000 onward. HeapAlloc went 1.44MB at 1000 batches to 1.457MB at 6000, so it is flat.
findings.discriminator: Pool created count stops at 400, equal to maxBatch, and the heap is flat after GC across 6000 batches. Every Get is matched by one Put, with no double-Put or lost buffers.

findings.mechanism: Renderer.index holds a rendered doc per invoice ID during a batch.
findings.cause: emptied at the end of every RenderBatch (delete loop at lines 86-89)
findings.evidence: Heap measured flat after GC over 6000 batches.
findings.discriminator: index is fully drained at the end of each batch, and IDs are unique per batch.
